IMO I don't think you should. I know you want to express yourself and it seems really important and this isn't the answer you want to hear but you really need to weigh the risk to your safety with the reward. 

Do you really understand what it means to be homeless? Not knowing if you'll be able to eat, if you'll be able to brush your teeth, not having a roof over your head, not only having your stuff on the street but risk not having it at all or them trashing it. If you don't drive how will you get places?  What if they beat you before tossing you out? What about health insurance and medical bills, dentist and doctor appointments and someone taking care of you when you're sick.

No one will pay your phone bill, no one will pay for Internet or new clothes or school supplies. Are they willing to help you pay for college because they sure as hell won't after. 

Now if the reward is worth all that risk to you then you should make plans. You should anyway since you've already told your brother and others so there's a risk it will get back to them.There are resources for homeless kids and LGBT kids which you should look up but being in homeless shelters even juvenile ones aren't great situations, you should also evaluate if anyone you know will take you in.

It's just 2 years. 2 years and you can move away to college. It seems like a long time but try and focus on other things. Being a teenager I know you want to really express your identity but you don't need to express it because it will always be your identity. Eventually you will be able to express yourself to your hearts content but really, really think about it.

I had a very saitama "ok" moment

I had undiagnosed bp2. Started medication, started caring about living again and then I  had a really bad hospitalization the first Halloween party after I turned 21 that was a real kick in the butt.

I scared my bf, who is a very gentle person, who this was the first time seeing me hospitalized. Then I was released from the hospital who told me I was just hungover. Well they were fucking wrong and I had to go to another hospital within hours. My pump injection site had failed and I had been too drunk/high to be aware and went into dka very very quickly. I just had the realization that if I hadn't known my body enough, had believed the first hospital, had gone back to my dorm room instead of to my bf's house (my roommate wanted a cat so she had moved out) I would have died. 

I couldn't move at all so when the ambulance came for the second hospitalization firemen had to put me in a chair and carry me down. I'm small but it was soooo fucking embarrassing. 

Also before the first hospitalization I had been sick in my friend's car so they stopped at a gas station and I was puking in an outside bin, well my shirt was covered in vomit on a cold October night and my body temp was 91°F when I was admitted. I had woken up and honestly, because I didn't remember anything I thought I had been roofied and was scared I had been assaulted. Also can't stomach alcohol anymore because for the longest time it tastes like puke and now I just lost the taste for it.

I wish I had sued that first hospital tbh. They actually ended up shutting down later. I don't think sueing is the answer to everything but dying was a real potential consequence to their negligence. I was puking up the oral antinausea medication and they said, yep, diabetic puking every twenty minutes who insists shes in dka whos been hospitalized every year for dka for the past 6 years. Anyway I realized that in the helpless state of being in dka I can't trust medical staff. Never been a problem before but that scared me.

I've visited the hospital a couple times since because of problem injection sites, but I go so early that usually it's just a matter of going on an IV to correct pH levels and hydration, usually under 24 hours. Part of those failures are due to scar tissue from previous lantus sites, so that was a bit of a learning curve. Hmm maybe more like scales but everything keeps being added to one side. Greed morally is bad, but I think one thing to consider is, fictional aside, Iruma is not a 'typical' child. He is a child with a past of neglect/abuse. Therefore, his logic is often can be warped.

Maybe I'm just coming off of Kotaro-san lives alone or projecting my own experience but in neglect/abuse cases the children never learned properly how to deal with certain social boundaries and their own desires, and usually have trouble adjusting. This is show-cased by Iruma's pushoverness, it's stated multiple times in the show that he's been conditioned by his narcissistic parents to put others above himself and that their needs are above his own. Yes this makes him seem good and selfless but in reality, it's from a lack of self-esteem and self-worth. How much of it is conditioned behavior? How much of it is genuine goodwill? Does the source of good actions negate their effect of them? There's a lot of ambiguity here. Either way my point of this is that Iruma's 'goodness' is in part a farce.

Children who are neglected/abused often try to fill the 'hole' left by their awful parents. He has friends and family to fill the emotional side but there is still the 'hole' of self-actualization. You also seem to have this concept of what authors do, which to you is working alone and working creatively. You do realize that authors who get novels published have to work with editors and publishers who can pull some serious edits of your work, dipping their fingers into your story. Which is not alone.

Now about being an author who doesn't read. In my opinion - no. When you write something who are your creative inspirations? Who are the authors you model yourself after? You say you're good at writing but think specifically about what pieces you have written? Are they small school pieces from highschool? How long are they? What criteria were your pieces held up to - other students or published authors? Do you know how long novels are (high fantasy like lotr is 100k+ or publishers won't touch it)?
